task: round 13 scan_hyp_gated_fusion (gated fusion focus; hikaggler 0.957 / mige551 0.959)
summary: No gated-fusion idea reaches R8. (1) The lever hikaggler describes is already in x138, and so in both finals #37 and #38. His words were 'the second model only on COLUMNS where the primary is uncertain'. x138's SECONDARY_LINK_MODE=low_margin_consensus (hard-set in cell 3 l.660-662, code in cell 4 _ensemble_replacements patch 3) does exactly this. For each target column of the edge-logit matrix it takes the primary's softmax top-2 margin m and sets the weight to 0.15*clamp((0.35-m)/0.35,0,1). The weight is 0 unless both models pick the same top parent. Detection has a two-seed logit blend (0.2 primary + 0.8 z-aligned secondary), plus a frame-level disagreement gate: the retention guard falls back to primary-only when blended/primary candidates < 0.90. (2) The only form x138 lacks is a voxel- or candidate-level detection gate. The exp60 dumps have no heatmaps and no per-model candidates: trainlab npz holds graphs and DeepCenter scores; edge_cache holds blended coords, low_coords and low_score, and empty edge arrays. So there is no CPU lab. Any detection change needs a GPU re-run: 2 kernels x ~1.95 h (exp60_a took 6,988 s), about 4 GPU-h and 4.5-5 h wall. (3) By construction a voxel gate barely moves the candidate set. Its uncertain band has to contain the threshold (p 0.969, logit ~3.43), so near-threshold voxels still get x138's blend. Only confident-disagreement voxels change, and at the frame level the retention guard already covers those. Net blended/primary candidates in non-fallback frames: 0.982 (44b6) and 0.995 (6bba). The bound for the related guard-off change is ~+0.005 lab with a likely sign <= 0 (I-222). The recall pool ceiling is +0.029 lab as an oracle, and 69% of the 6bba misses have no peak. Prior: 0.000 +- 0.001 public, P(display 0.955) ~0.05. Runtime cost ~0 (elementwise ops on maps already computed; < 1 min over ~100 clips). The idea sits inside the closed detector-blend / secondary-weight family (I-102, I-155, I-156). Honest answer: nothing to build before R8. Update I-126 to 'already in the base (edge side); detection-side variant deferred-after-deadline'. Finals unchanged.

findings.what: hikaggler's 'conditional two-model fusion' is already in x138, and so in #37 and #38. His phrase is 'the second model only on COLUMNS where the primary is uncertain'. x138's edge fusion low_margin_consensus does the same thing: for each target column of the n_src x n_tgt edge-logit matrix it computes softmax over sources (dim=0) and the primary top-2 margin m, then sets blend weight = 0.15 * clamp((0.35 - m)/0.35, 0, 1), and 0 unless primary and secondary agree on the top parent. The weight is applied per column (view(1,1,-1)). The secondary logits are z-aligned to the primary (mean/std, ratio clamp 0.5-2). mige551's 'two-seed logit blend' and FOYSAL's 'extra view only where models disagree' map to x138's 0.8 detection blend plus the frame-level retention guard. So I-126 is not an untried lever for us. Its natural form (edge columns) is part of the stack that scores 0.953-0.954.

findings.what: G1, a voxel-level uncertainty band gate on detection (the only unimplemented form of hikaggler's idea). Mechanism: inside the retention-guard block (cell 4 _guard_new string, the 'blended_det = ...' anchor, which occurs once) replace the global blend with blended_det = primary_det + 0.80 * g(primary_det) * (secondary_det_aligned - primary_det), where g is a smooth band in logit space, e.g. 1 on [lo, hi] = [1.5, 5.5] around the threshold logit ln(0.96875/0.03125) = 3.43 with 0.5-logit ramps, and 0 outside. The guard then counts candidates on the gated map, as now. Smallest builder patch: --patch detgate (x138 base; one anchor inside the _guard_new literal, env BIOHUB_DETGATE_LO/HI; not applied in K2 builds, so they stay byte-identical; fail-soft = on exception keep the original blend). Expected gain arithmetic: near-threshold voxels keep x138's blend by construction, so only confident-disagreement voxels change. These are (a) peaks where the primary is confidently high and the secondary low, which the blend suppresses (at frame level the guard already rescues these in 44b6's 563/1,700 fallback frames), and (b) secondary-only peaks where the primary is confidently low, which get removed (fewer nodes). In non-fallback frames the net candidate difference is only 1.8% (44b6, 329,646 vs 335,525) and 0.5% (6bba, 803,274 vs 807,232). At the metric's node factor, +-1% nodes is about -+0.0009 on J, so node effects alone are below +-0.002 lab. Recall side: 668 missing GT nodes = +0.029 lab as an oracle. Only 31% of 6bba misses have any raw local max within 5 um, so any two-peak-detector fusion reaches at most ~+0.01 as an oracle, and realistically at the few-% precision of such arms (raw-maxima arm ~-0.03) <= +0.002 lab = <= +0.0003 public at the ~1/6 transfer. The related I-222 (force the blend in fallback frames) is bounded at ~+0.005 lab with a likely sign <= 0. Localisation at confident voxels is the lowrefine class (scored neutral). Central public 0.000, sd ~0.001; P(display 0.955) ~0.05. Runtime on the ~100-clip hidden run: 3-4 elementwise ops on a map that already exists, per frame (~10^4 frames), < 1 min; no extra model pass (secondary 8-view TTA is already computed).

findings.what: G2, a candidate-level retention guard (max-union), which would replace the frame-level switch. The map becomes torch.where(primary_det > hi, torch.maximum(blended_det, primary_det), blended_det), so the blend keeps its peaks and gains the primary's confident peaks that it suppressed; the frame-level fallback is then removed. Mechanism: the frame switch throws away the blend's extra detections in fallback frames (44b6 33% of frames), and keeps no confident primary peaks in blended frames. Arithmetic: in 44b6 fallback frames the blend has 21.9% fewer candidates (136,124 vs 174,321). Taking the union there keeps the primary's set plus the blend's extras. Blend > primary happens in 377/1,700 (44b6) and 1,706/3,900 (6bba) frames, so the node count rises by an unknown fraction. At the metric's node factor, each +1% nodes costs ~0.0009 J unless offset by annotated TP edges (base match 0.79% in 44b6 vs 5.20% in 6bba, so the sign flips by embryo, as every node lever on x138 did: I-147, I-148). Max-union also creates duplicate peaks where the two maxima are offset by more than the pool radius, i.e. FP nodes. Prior: public -0.001 .. +0.0005, central slightly negative. Runtime ~0.
